name: Digital literacy among farmers (%)
reason: The gap was attacked using the supplied official statistical instruments, agricultural-sector pages, the CGIAR farmer study, and the additional Beni Suef case-study material. None affirmatively supplies a national percentage of Egyptian farmers who are digitally literate; the closest numeric evidence has both scope and construct mismatches.

answer.abstain_reason: Retrieved evidence provides subnational, non-equivalent proxies or barriers rather than a nationally published percentage of Egyptian farmers who are digitally literate.
answer.source_title: CGIAR, Digital Literacy Training to Promote Diffusion of Digital Agricultural Tools to Smallholder Farmers
answer.construct_note: The closest admissible source reports that 52 percent of sampled farmers identified general digital literacy as a key challenge; it is a perceived barrier/digital-illiteracy measure among an intervention sample in Minya and Benisuef, not a national percentage of farmers who are digitally literate. The additional Beni Suef case-study figures concern ICT/IoT knowledge, training, and mobile-app use, not digital literacy, and are T5 and subnational.
answer.scale_evidence: The CGIAR policy note describes a target population of about 4,000 smallholder farmers across Minya and Benisuef; the T5 presentation describes a case study of 128 farmers in Tawa village, Biba, Beni Suef.
answer.rung_argument: No threshold rung is proposed: none of the supplied pages publishes a national Egyptian farmer digital-literacy percentage. CAPMAS materials retrieved are survey instruments/data dictionaries for households or agricultural establishments, not a published farmer digital-literacy result. The CGIAR source supplies only a two-governorate barrier finding, while the other farmer ICT evidence is an inadmissible T5 local case study.
answer.negative_finding: Level 1 requires a published value for the named construct; the supplied pages do not establish a national percentage of Egyptian farmers who are digitally literate.
answer.search_trail: Independently reviewed the retrieved CAPMAS agricultural-census form (Source 1), CAPMAS household ICT survey data dictionary and questionnaire/instructions (Sources 2–4), CAPMAS social-accounting-matrix publication (Source 5), CGIAR/IFPRI Egypt smallholder RCT policy note (Source 6), Ministry of Agriculture pages (Sources 8–9), and the Beni Suef ICT case-study presentation (Source 10). Source 6 supplies a two-governorate perceived digital-literacy barrier; Source 10 supplies local ICT knowledge/training/use measures but is T5. No supplied page provides the named national farmer digital-literacy rate.
